question: What is the main goal of health education in nursing?

options.B: Reducing the cost of hospital equipment

explanation: Spot on! Our core job as nurses is to help people stay well and stop illnesses before they even start. Keep it up! [learn more](GNS112_U2_T6#GNS112_U2_T6_h1)

question: Why is a quick chat with a patient at the bedside considered health education?

options.A: Every clinical interaction is an opportunity to share knowledge
options.B: Patients prefer talking over reading heavy medical textbooks
options.C: Hospital management requires a daily quota of conversations
options.D: It gives the nurse a break from heavy physical tasks

explanation: Exactly! Teaching doesn't only happen in a formal classroom. Even a brief chat while checking vitals helps a patient understand their health better. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T6#GNS112_U2_T6_h1)

question: Which teaching principle means we should start with what matters most to the patient right now?
explanation: You got it! When we talk about things that touch their daily lives and immediate worries, patients listen and learn much faster. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T6#GNS112_U2_T6_h2)

question: Why do we let patients try out a new physical skill themselves during teaching?

options.A: It ensures the patient can safely perform the task on their own
options.B: It is required to update the electronic health record
options.C: It prevents the patient from asking difficult questions
options.D: It makes the nurse finish their shift much faster

explanation: Brilliant! Having them practice physically builds their confidence and proves they can handle it safely once they go home. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T6#GNS112_U2_T6_h2)

question: What is the first thing a nurse should check before starting a teaching session?

options.B: The personal hobbies of the patient

explanation: Spot on! If a patient is in severe pain or exhausted, teaching won't stick. Always check if they are ready first. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T6#GNS112_U2_T6_h3)

question: A patient scheduled for discharge is crying and upset after a new diagnosis. What should the nurse do?

options.A: Postpone detailed instructions until the patient's emotional readiness improves
options.B: Ask a family member to take over all future health responsibilities
options.C: Hand the patient a textbook and tell them to read it alone
options.D: Proceed quickly with the teaching so the patient leaves on time

explanation: Well reasoned! High emotions block learning. Comforting the patient and waiting until they are calmer is always the right clinical call. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T6#GNS112_U2_T6_h3)

question: What do we call the method where the nurse shows a procedure and the patient does it back?
explanation: Correct! Showing them first and then watching them do it lets you spot and fix mistakes right away. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T6#GNS112_U2_T6_h4)

question: Why should nurses avoid heavy medical jargon when explaining things to patients?

options.A: It causes patients to doubt the nurse's clinical training
options.B: It confuses patients and hinders their understanding of home care
options.C: It takes too much time to pronounce difficult words
options.D: It is considered unprofessional by hospital administrators

explanation: You nailed it. Plain, simple language helps patients truly grasp their care without feeling overwhelmed. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T6#GNS112_U2_T6_h4)

question: Why is a patient simply nodding and smiling an unreliable sign that they understand?

options.B: Patients cannot hear the nurse while nodding
options.C: Patients often nod out of politeness or fear rather than comprehension
options.D: It means the patient disagrees with the plan

explanation: Exactly. Many people will just nod politely to a nurse or doctor even when they are totally confused. Always double-check! [learn more](GNS112_U2_T6#GNS112_U2_T6_h5)

question: Which of these is NOT a barrier to patient education?

options.D: High anxiety and fear of diagnosis

explanation: Spot on! A quiet, comfortable space actually helps learning happen, whereas pain, anxiety, and language gaps get in the way. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T6#GNS112_U2_T6_h5)

question: What is the main purpose of using the teach-back method?

options.A: To fulfill strict insurance billing rules
options.B: To confirm whether the patient truly understands the instructions
options.C: To give the nurse a break from talking
options.D: To test the patient's long-term memory capacity

explanation: Correct! Asking them to explain it back in their own words is the best way to make sure they got the right message. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T6#GNS112_U2_T6_h6)

question: After teaching a patient about wound care, what must the nurse document in the patient's notes?

options.A: Nothing, as verbal education does not require charting
options.B: Details of what was taught, the method used, and the patient's response
options.C: A summary of the nurse's personal feelings about the patient
options.D: Only the date and the nurse's personal signature

explanation: Well done! If it wasn't charted, legally it wasn't done. Always record what you taught and how the patient responded. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T6#GNS112_U2_T6_h6)

question: Why are nurses in a great position to act as health educators?

options.A: They receive no medical training and speak like ordinary people
options.B: They are the only healthcare professionals legally allowed to teach
options.C: They spend continuous time at the bedside interacting with patients
options.D: They control the hospital budget for educational supplies

explanation: Spot on! Because nurses are always around, we can break teaching down into small, easy steps over time. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T6#GNS112_U2_T6_h7)

question: What does a nurse do when acting as a facilitator of health education?

options.A: Punishes patients who fail to follow their diet plan
options.B: Writes medical textbooks for nursing schools
options.D: Guides patients toward healthier choices instead of just lecturing them

explanation: You got it! A good facilitator walks alongside the patient, encouraging them to take charge of their own health journey. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T6#GNS112_U2_T6_h7)
